brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.evidence: piece:0,0,0;full plus piece:1,0,0;half-n, held together by jointBolt:0#0,0#0. Covers on both tops and caps on all 7 open edges.

bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (a full bin with 3 compartments) and bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-half-n-half. The bins drop into their sockets and sit under removable top covers. The check confirms fit only, not how easy they are to lift out.
drawer:0#1,0#cut sits on the south cut face of the half base.
handle:0,0,0;top is on the full base's top cover, with 3 inserts the configurator added automatically. I made no claim about how much weight it can carry.

finish.summary: Small portable organizer, 19 parts: a full and a half hex base bolted together, 2 bins (one with 3 compartments), a drawer in the half base, top covers, a carry handle on the full base and caps on every open edge. check_build: no issues and meshClash is clear.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
